summary: A list of the people and organisations who care about a project, programme or operation, and how much say each has in it.
example: Quality Check Rollout stakeholders: the analytics partner cares a lot and has some say; the transport contractor has little of either.
definition: The stakeholders of one project, programme or operation, and how much power each holds over it: a stakeholder is anyone who can affect the work or is affected by it. A map is scoped to one project, programme or operation (TAXONOMY.md, what a programme carries), and each entry names either a Resource from the catalogue or one of the work's beneficiary groups (group), exactly one, so a party is declared once and scored separately on every project, programme or operation it touches. Each stakeholder is identified first, as primary (directly affected) or secondary (indirectly affected, Clarkson), and placed later by influence and interest, whose grid gives the engagement approach (Mendelow): manage closely, keep satisfied, keep informed, monitor. A stakeholder map is not the list of roles a project staffs (those are its resources), not the beneficiary groups (who gains value), and not a list of persons.

/spec/scope.guide: The project, programme or operation this map is about, by kind and id. Nothing else can be a scope: a stakeholder has a stake in a project, programme or operation. Define the work first.

poor.why: A team is not a project, programme or operation, and a map scoped to one is refused. Scope it to the project, programme or operation the team runs.

/metadata/name.guide: The work's name followed by "stakeholders", so the map is found beside the work.

poor.why: Every map would be called this; name the work it is about.

/spec/entries.guide: One entry per stakeholder, each a Resource from the catalogue, scored at most once. A party need not be one the work draws on: a party with power over a project is often not part of it. An entry with no score is a stakeholder named and not yet placed, which is a real state.

/spec/entries/-/group.guide: A beneficiary group of the work, when the stakeholder is the people it is for. Pick one of the groups the work already names; there is no need to record them again as a Resource. An entry names a group or a resource, not both.

poor.text: delivering-members, also added as a Resource
poor.why: The same people recorded twice. Name the group here.

/spec/entries/-/resource.guide: The catalogue entry for the stakeholder: a role, unit, party, system or facility. External bodies count. When the party is not in the catalogue, declare it there first. A group of the people the work is for goes in group instead.

poor.why: A person, not a role or a party. Cartograph names roles, and people hold them (D27).
Not a catalogue entry, and too broad to place on the grid. Name the unit or the role.

/spec/entries/-/stake.guide: What this party cares about in this work, in one sentence. Influence and interest say how much; this says what. It is about this work, not about who they are.
good: Wants fewer rejected loads, and no slower intake at busy depots.
Must sign off any change to how member delivery records are kept.

poor.why: Who they are, which the catalogue entry already says. Say what they care about here.
How much, which interest already scores. Say what the interest is in.

/spec/entries/-/owner.guide: The role that manages the relationship with this stakeholder, from the Resource catalogue. Never a person. How and when to engage them belongs to the communications plan.

poor.why: A person, not a role: Cartograph names roles, and people hold them.

/spec/entries/-/tier.guide: Primary if the work affects them directly, secondary if indirectly (Clarkson). A separate question from influence and interest: a secondary stakeholder can still hold a great deal of power.

/spec/entries/-/influence.guide: How much this stakeholder can change what happens, from 1 (little) to 3 (a great deal). Leave it blank until it is assessed; a guess placed as fact misleads the grid.

/spec/entries/-/interest.guide: How much this stakeholder cares what happens, from 1 (little) to 3 (a great deal). Leave it blank until it is assessed.

checks.stakeholders-identified: Name each party with a stake in the work, from the Resource catalogue: those it affects and those who can affect it.
checks.stakeholders-placed: Place each stakeholder by influence and interest, one to three each, so the approach to them follows from the grid.
